summary: A model-heavy week: Meta shipped Muse Wonder, its first frontier-class model, Google opened Gemini 4 Argon to developers, and Microsoft unveiled Maia 300 as its main in-house inference chip at OCP. Anthropic disclosed it replaced Git (Scion/Antique) after merges hit 30k/day, while Karpathy's 'capability funnel' post framed how unevenly frontier ability is felt. Space news was mostly schedule slips (Neutron to 2027, New Glenn targeting December) plus a planned Starship ship-catch on Flight 15; bio was quiet apart from a reported FNIH/NCI $200M cancer-vaccine initiative. Verification: 25 checked, 9 passed, 12 fixed, 4 dropped; 3 entities added.

highlights.title: Meta ships Muse Wonder, its first frontier-class model, at $4/$20 per M tokens
highlights.detail: Oct 12, 2026: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Wonder (API, $4/$20 per M tokens) and Muse Wonder Full (Muse Code subscribers), claiming parity with Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra and leading on its MemoryBench 'active memory' eval (self-reported).

highlights.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Argon to developers at $2/$10; prices double in December
highlights.detail: Oct 13, 2026: Gemini 4 Argon, Google's long-horizon reasoning model, became broadly available via the Gemini API, AI Studio and Antigravity (Ultra tier) plus the Gemini app for Pro/Ultra subscribers; introductory pricing is $2/$10 per M tokens through Nov 30, doubling in December. A less-restricted cyber variant requires separate approval for vetted defenders.

highlights.title: JetBrains open-sources Mellum2.1, a 12B MoE coding-agent model trained with RL
highlights.detail: Oct 8, 2026 (backfill, one day before window): JetBrains released Mellum2.1 under Apache-2.0, a 12B-parameter (~2.5B active) MoE for coding agents, post-trained with RL in real repo environments using shell/file-edit tools and test-based rewards; 47.0% SWE-bench Verified (self-reported).

highlights.detail: Oct 1, 2026 (backfill): Cloudflare released open-weight (Apache-2.0) Clef (27B) and Clef-flash (9B), which take a state plus a schema of typed questions and return probabilities over allowed answers; similar 'decision' models reported from Liquid AI and Microsoft point to a small-model class for routing/verification in agent pipelines (vendor claims).

highlights.title: Anthropic replaces Git with in-house Scion/Antique as merges hit 30k/day
highlights.detail: Oct 13, 2026: Anthropic's engineering blog says merged changes rose from ~2,500/day (May) to 30,000+/day (Sep), forcing a custom server-centric source-control system (Scion) with an AI-assisted review tool (Antique), migrated in ~five months; Scion reportedly uses 200x less CPU/memory than the git mirror fleet (vendor-reported).

highlights.title: XPeng: IRON humanoid goes on sale H2 2027 after in-store pilots
highlights.detail: Oct 12, 2026: XPeng president Brian Gu told the Forbes Global CEO Conference IRON will be sold from H2 2027, after working as store sales assistants/receptionists from early 2027; it runs on XPeng's in-house Turing chip.

highlights.detail: Oct 9, 2026: NYT reported a ~$200M public-private Therapeutic Cancer Vaccines Initiative run by FNIH and NCI to build shared trial networks for treatment vaccines, expected to launch in December; Moderna closed up ~14% (coinciding with its Nasdaq-100 re-entry; no direct funding to Moderna confirmed).

highlights.title: BioNTech's individualized cancer-vaccine program narrows to pancreatic Ph2
highlights.detail: Oct 2026: Analysis notes BioNTech/Genentech terminated the Ph2 ctDNA+ colorectal autogene cevumeran trial (Aug 28) after a DSMB flagged an OS imbalance, and the Ph2 IMcode004 urothelial trial was discontinued earlier in 2026, leaving pancreatic IMcode003 as the main active study, in contrast to Moderna/Merck's Ph3 intismeran (full data at ESMO Oct 24).

highlights.title: Paradromics Connexus: first human implant in Connect-One study (backfill)
highlights.detail: Jun 17, 2026 (backfill): Paradromics and U-Michigan Health completed the first Connexus implant in the FDA-approved Connect-One early feasibility study (ALS/motor neuron disease; speech/text goal), complementing this month's sheep-durability data.

payload.new_value: First human Connexus implant (Jun 17, 2026; Connect-One EFS)

highlights.title: Rocket Lab pushes Neutron's first launch to 2027
highlights.detail: Oct 14, 2026: Rocket Lab announced an adjusted Neutron development schedule, moving the reusable medium-lift rocket's inaugural launch into 2027.

highlights.title: Starship Flight 15 to attempt first ship tower catch ~late November
highlights.detail: Oct 11, 2026: Musk said Flight 15 will try to catch the Starship upper stage with the tower, roughly four to six weeks out, with Flight 16 targeting booster and ship reflight.

highlights.title: Falcon 9 booster B1088 flies its 20th mission
highlights.detail: Oct 12, 2026: B1088 flew its 20th flight (Starlink 15-25 from Vandenberg) and landed on OCISLY.

highlights.title: Blue Origin targets December for New Glenn return to flight
highlights.detail: Oct 7-9, 2026 (backfill): Bezos said Blue Origin is targeting December for New Glenn's return to flight with Blue Ring aboard; the vehicle has been grounded since the Apr 19, 2026 flight-3 upper-stage anomaly. December is a target, not a confirmed date.

highlights.title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 as its primary in-house inference chip
highlights.detail: Oct 12, 2026 (OCP Global Summit): Microsoft's third-gen Maia 300 (TSMC N2P, 288 GB HBM4) becomes its main inference platform, deploying from 2027 at multi-GW scale; Microsoft claims 40% more tokens per MW than leading GPU systems (vendor figures).

highlights.title: Karpathy: LLM capability perception is now a steep 'funnel'
highlights.detail: Oct 11, 2026: Karpathy argued awareness of LLM capability forms a funnel, from billions with little exposure to ~thousands with frontier-internal access, driven by task horizon, verifiable domains and paid/internal access tiers.

payload.thesis: Frontier capability is concentrating among a tiny set of users in verifiable domains; free-tier experience badly understates what agents can do.

highlights.title: Nvidia commits $250M of compute to UK agentic-AI safety research
highlights.detail: Oct 14, 2026: Nvidia pledged ~$50M/yr of compute for five years for UK research on AI-agent security and open-model vulnerabilities (Imperial College among recipients).
